Better noise calibration exposed an inference problem

All 36 nonlinear posterior runs pass the finite convergence screen. Worst Rhat 1.0093; minimum bulk/tail ESS 821/556. Four chains per case; 2,000 retained transitions per chain, extended to 4,000 for one floor-control case. Passing these checks cannot prove global exploration or physical-model correctness.

The neural model's apparent disadvantage largely disappears when we average over plausible motions instead of selecting the highest-density path. Neural and constant noise give practically the same reconstruction. This is evidence for better inference, not a demonstrated neural-model advantage.

Same six images, same physics, same marginalized forces

The experiment repeats the original four truth conditions × three seeds × three noise models. Geometry, appearance, camera, FEM, six-substep integrator, frozen noise weights, independent fine reference data and all density normalizers are unchanged. The benchmark was already inspected; this is an inference comparison, not a blind test.

Means over six stochastic-condition cases sharing three underlying seeds. The neural–constant difference is only 0.019 mm; maximum reported per-coordinate mean MCSE across the study is 0.124 mm. No credible superiority claim follows from this difference. Central component intervals use no conformal multiplier and do not target simultaneous whole-gap coverage.

Why calibration made the old point estimates worse

Correcting an overestimated diffusion amplitude tightened the mechanics prior and introduced more realistic state dependence. The most probable complete path can then move toward a region with higher probability density but less total probability mass. Covariance and drag normalizers matter in a path with 1,440 velocity coordinates. Removing them would change the model; integrating over paths addresses the point-estimator problem.

The calibration-only control uses the same final numerical operators. Across three pulse-plus-noise seeds, old/calibrated/oracle neural MAP errors are 3.160/3.622/3.606 mm. Even the exact analytic amplitude gives almost the same MAP error as the calibrated network. Remaining amplitude approximation error is therefore not the main explanation.

On the declared development case, restarting optimization from the posterior mean returns to the original mode: objective 1610.291050 → 1610.290951, gap error 4.211 → 4.231 mm. The posterior average has 2.172 mm error. Tighter local optimization does not recover that average.

Posterior averaging does not improve every realization. Four of six stochastic neural cases worsen, while the average improves because two cases improve substantially. The old model also has a restricted force basis, fixed scene assumptions and an independent discrepancy floor. This audit does not attribute every remaining reconstruction error to MAP alone.

What changed in inference

The old sampler made small random moves and mixed poorly in damping. The replacement uses Gaussian-reference split Hamiltonian proposals, with exact mechanics gradients. A local image approximation makes proposals cheaper; the full nonlinear renderer and normalized marginalized-force density decide acceptance. Step size adapts only in discarded warmup, then freezes. Every state coordinate, gap coordinate, conditional force mean, and applicable force variance/normalizer is monitored.

Some proposals have large energy errors or invalid physical intermediates and are rejected. Counts are preserved per case; independent smaller-step checks are in step-checks/. These are numerical sensitivity checks, not model tuning. Force uncertainty averages both the conditional covariance and variation between inferred trajectories.

Independent numerical replication

Both independently seeded smaller-step runs pass all Rhat/ESS monitors and have no invalid proposals or large energy errors. The floor case changes gap RMSE by 0.010 mm. The initial neural case changes 2.172 → 2.247 mm; two of 84 coordinates marginally exceed an approximate batch-MCSE/Bonferroni agreement threshold (maximum |z|=3.553, threshold 3.434). Both cached full targets reproduce within 5.5×10⁻¹².

Both unchanged neural kernels were then extended once to 4,000 retained states per chain, without further adaptation. Both pass every convergence monitor, with no invalid/large-energy proposals. At that fixed budget, maximum |z|=3.157, with 0 of 84 coordinates exceeding the same approximate threshold. Gap RMSE is 2.179/2.221 mm. The initial borderline comparison and longer-run results are preserved in replica-comparison-initial.json, replica-comparison-extended.json and extended-checks/. These supplementary estimates do not replace or select outcomes in the frozen 36-case benchmark. Batch-MCSE agreement does not prove calibration.

Evidence and limitations

All numerical results · Comparison table · Hashes and run provenance · Equations and algorithms · Frozen protocol

94 numerical tests pass. The public Actions artifacts retain full latent chains and proposal errors for 30 days; code, fixed seeds, exact observed images, portable joint draws, all-coordinate diagnostics and reproduction commands remain in the repository. Raw posterior intervals are conditional on a known synthetic scene and frozen diffusion model. Repeated-realization posterior calibration, time/mesh sensitivity, unknown cameras/geometry, contact and real-video reconstruction remain open.
